subject: history
title: Why did the First World War start?
brief: Year 8 history, why did the First World War start?

slides.alt: Slide 1, title: Why did the First World War start? Year 8 history. Enquiry: which cause mattered most? A row of falling dominoes above the year 1914.

Slide 2, objectives: The enquiry. I can explain four long-term causes of the war. I can describe how the murder at Sarajevo led to war in six weeks. I can reach a supported judgement on which cause mattered most.
Slide 3, starter: A spark or a pile of dry wood? A forest fire starts from one small spark. What really caused the fire: the spark, or the dry wood? Think, pair, share. A spark above a stack of logs.

Slide 4, vocabulary: Key words. Alliance: an agreement between countries to support each other. Mobilise: to get an army ready for war. Ultimatum: a final demand, with a threat if it is refused. Neutral: not taking any side in a war.

Slide 5: Long-term causes, M.A.I.N. Militarism: great powers built up huge armies and navies, and Britain and Germany raced to build battleships. Alliances: Europe split into two armed groups. Imperialism: competition for colonies and trade created distrust. Nationalism: strong national pride, and Slav peoples in the Balkans wanting their own states.

Slide 6: Two alliance systems. The Triple Entente of Britain, France and Russia, and the Triple Alliance of Germany, Austria-Hungary and Italy. Two other promises: Russia saw itself as Serbia’s protector, and Britain had promised in 1839 to protect Belgium.

Slide 7: The spark, Sarajevo, 28 June 1914. Archduke Franz Ferdinand, heir to the throne of Austria-Hungary, and his wife Sophie were shot dead in Sarajevo, Bosnia, by Gavrilo Princip, a Bosnian Serb nationalist who wanted Bosnia free of Austria-Hungary.

Slide 8: Six weeks from assassination to world war. A timeline: 28 June, Franz Ferdinand is assassinated; 28 July, Austria-Hungary declares war on Serbia; 30 July, Russia mobilises its army; 1 August, Germany declares war on Russia; 3 August, Germany declares war on France; 4 August, Germany invades Belgium and Britain declares war.

Slide 9, sort: Sort the causes into long-term causes, built up over many years, and short-term causes, in the weeks before the war. Cards: the naval race, the murder at Sarajevo, rivalry over colonies, Austria-Hungary’s ultimatum to Serbia, the alliance system, Russia mobilises, Slav nationalism, Germany invades Belgium.

Slide 10, open response: Your judgement. Which cause mattered most? Rank militarism, alliances, imperialism, nationalism and the assassination in five numbered slots from most to least important, then explain your top choice in a paragraph starting ‘The most important cause was … because …’.

pages.alt: Reading worksheet for Why did the First World War start?: a short text explaining how the murder at Sarajevo, Austria-Hungary’s ultimatum, Russia’s mobilisation and Germany’s invasion of neutral Belgium led to war, followed by four questions on the text.

answers.alt: Answer key for Why did the First World War start?: Austria-Hungary blamed Serbia; Russia mobilised to protect the Slav peoples; Germany’s plan went through neutral Belgium, which Britain had promised in 1839 to protect; evidence of militarism is the naval race or plans to move millions of soldiers.
